text:
maggie: quick check — onboarding `athena-7b` smoke showed missing manifest fields (no `vocab_uri`), weights are in gs://redwood-models/athena-7b/v1/ but CI still complains. anyone seen this pattern before?
nisha: saw something similar with a typo in the manifest key. can you paste the top-level of the config.json?
maggie: pasted below:
```json
{
  "name": "athena-7b",
  "version": "v1",
  "weights_uri": "gs://redwood-models/athena-7b/v1/weights.pt",
  "tokenizer": { "type": "sentencepiece" }
}
```
oliver: ah, no `vocab_uri` — our schema expects either `vocab_uri` or `tokenizer.vocab_file`. CI lint rule `tokenizer-vocab-presence` enforces that. engci-bot should have flagged earlier?
engci-bot: lint error: `tokenizer-vocab-presence` failed on sources: config.json line 1 — missing `vocab_uri` or `tokenizer.vocab_file`. See https://ci.redwood/lintruns/5543
maggie: weird, I did get a lint email but it got buried. ok adding `tokenizer.vocab_file`. quick q: for sentencepiece we usually point to `spm.model` in GCS — is that `vocab_file` or still `vocab_uri`?
samir: convention: top-level `vocab_uri` is preferred for legacy models. Newer ones should use `tokenizer.vocab_file`. both accepted by runtime; schema requires at least one.
kai: also watch out for `pad_id` behavior — sentencepiece sometimes uses id=0 for <pad> but our runtime expects pad_id to be present when not 0. If missing, downstream padding can shift tokens.
maggie: noted. I'll add both to avoid ambiguity. new snippet:
```json
"tokenizer": {
  "type": "sentencepiece",
  "vocab_file": "gs://redwood-models/athena-7b/v1/spm.model",
  "pad_id": 1
}
```
nisha: :thumbsup: after you push, can you kick off the `config-schema-check` job (or re-run the asset-gate)? I'll watch for the gate failure and approve if green.
maggie: pushed manifest update and reran gate: https://ci.redwood/lintruns/5544 — it still errors but different message: `weights-uri-not-indexed`
oliver: that usually means the weights blob exists but index file missing for sharded checkpoints. do a quick ls of the weights path and make sure `index.json` or `manifest.sha256` present.
maggie: gs ls output shows `weights.pt`, `weights.pt.1`, and `shard_map.json` but no `index.json`
samir: we recently changed the expected name from `shard_map.json` -> `index.json` in the ingestion pipeline. older uploads still have shard_map. two options: re-upload index.json (preferred), or add `weights_index: shard_map.json` to config.json to be backward-compatible.
kai: yeah, add the alias for now so we don't block the rollout. but create a ticket to re-ingest with canonical `index.json` name.
maggie: done — added `weights_index: "shard_map.json"` and re-run gate. engci-bot shows one remaining warning: `tokenizer-padid-default` set to warn (pad_id=1 is nonstandard). is that something we should fix now?
engci-bot: warning: `tokenizer-padid-default` — pad_id not equal to 0; runtime will treat pad id as provided. See docs: https://docs.redwood/inference/tokenizers#pad-id
nisha: acceptable for this model for now. record in the onboarding notes that pad_id=1 and add to the model's `compatibility_notes`.
maggie: added note in the model metadata and re-ran. gate now passes. thanks all for quick help :raised_hands: 
oliver: nice — follow-up: please file a small PR to the ingestion tooling to accept `shard_map.json` as alias for `index.json` for one release cycle so old uploads don't break until we re-ingest.
samir: will take that. also I'll add a CI check to surface the missing index name earlier (pre-commit hook).
maggie: perfect. closing the loop — will ping when re-ingest is done.
kai: cheers, and add a short note to the release playbook about tokenizer pad quirks so infra oncall sees it next time.
maggie: will do. thanks!
